seoTitle: Message Delivery Failure and Retry Journey Example
seoDescription: What should happen when a message fails to reach its destination? This flow classifies the failure and decides between a retry, a fallback or a full stop.

seoTitle: Communication Obligation Closure and Escalation Map
seoDescription: Models how a communication obligation is closed once delivery attempts reach an outcome, and how the cases that could not be met are escalated instead.

seoTitle: Capturing Permission With an Explicit Scope Record
seoDescription: How a permission decision becomes an auditable record of what was authorised, by purpose, channel and scope. Follow the validate, activate or reject path.

seoTitle: Communication Preference Capture Lifecycle Journey
seoDescription: Shows how a declared preference is recorded and used to personalise permitted communication, in a store built so preference can never become permission.

seoTitle: Preference Change Recalculation Customer Journey
seoDescription: When someone changes a preference, what happens to messages already queued? This flow recalculates active journey instances and suppresses or adapts each.
reviewReason: Close neighbour of CON-34, which also models a preference change triggering a recalculation; CON-33 covers preferences in general and CON-34 covers frequency only.

seoTitle: Communication Frequency Change Lifecycle Journey
seoDescription: Examine how a frequency preference recalculates the cadence of optional messaging, applies prospectively and leaves required messages untouched.
reviewReason: Close neighbour of CON-33, the general preference-change recalculation journey; this record is the frequency-specific case.

seoTitle: Consent and Permission Change Enforcement Journey
seoDescription: A permission change has to stop affected communication at once. This journey models immediate enforcement first, then propagation to the other systems.

seoTitle: Channel Contactability and Reachability Journey Map
seoDescription: Tracks whether a channel can still reach a person, separately from whether it may, holding route health per contact point so sending avoids what is broken.

seoTitle: Communication Suppression State Journey Example
seoDescription: Every reason a message is not sent becomes an explicit, scoped, releasable state. Review how a suppression opens, is re-evaluated and is finally released.
reviewReason: Close neighbour of CON-39, which also holds messaging back; CON-38 records any suppression reason as state while CON-39 is a time-bound cooldown on optional messaging.

seoTitle: Messaging Cooldown and Re-evaluation Journey Map
seoDescription: Models a temporary hold on optional messaging after a trigger: how the cooldown is scoped, when it is re-evaluated and why permission stays intact.
reviewReason: Close neighbour of CON-38, the general suppression-state journey; this record covers the time-bound cooldown case only.

seoTitle: Permission Conflict and Fail-Safe Hold Journey
seoDescription: When two systems disagree about permission, optional messaging stays closed. Follow the fail-safe hold, evidence-based reconciliation and restore path.

seoTitle: Establishing Entity Ownership With an Explicit Act
seoDescription: How an accountable owner is established by an explicit act rather than inferred. The flow validates the requesting authority, then assigns or rejects it.

seoTitle: Ownership Transfer Request and Validation Journey
seoDescription: Proposing a future controller without disturbing the one an entity currently has. See how the request is validated, left pending acceptance, or rejected.

seoTitle: Ownership Transfer Acceptance and Revalidation Map
seoDescription: An acceptance made today must still match the transfer proposed. See how the request version is revalidated and then executed or allowed to expire.

seoTitle: Ownership Cutover Without an Uncontrolled Entity
seoDescription: Moving control between two parties while the entity is never left uncontrolled. Follow the new owner assignment and the reconciliation of the old one.

seoTitle: Granting Scoped Authority on an Owner's Behalf
seoDescription: Letting somebody act on an owner's behalf inside a boundary, without moving anything. Review how the scope is defined and the grant issued or refused.

seoTitle: Temporary Delegation Expiry and Renewal Journey Map
seoDescription: Borrowed authority has to end at its boundary. This flow checks the boundary still belongs to a delegation that exists, then revokes, extends or restores.

seoTitle: Delegation Revocation and Retained Access Journey
seoDescription: Taking back exactly what was lent and nothing else. The journey removes capabilities that exist because of the delegation, preserving independent access.

seoTitle: Protecting an Entity When Its Owner Is Unavailable
seoDescription: What holds an entity safely when its owner cannot act? This flow protects the ownership state and works towards recovery rather than the nearest party.

seoTitle: Data Intake, Format Detection and Parsing Journey
seoDescription: How a submitted dataset is identified, parsed and brought into a stable readable form, or rejected, before anything real is touched. Follow each branch.

seoTitle: Schema and Semantic Data Validation Journey Map
seoDescription: Checks parsed data against the target's schema and business rules, record by record, then accepts, rejects or quarantines it. Examine every branch here.

seoTitle: Impact Preview and Approval Before a Data Change
seoDescription: Before a mutation runs, what would it actually do? This flow builds the impact preview so approval attaches to real effects, then confirms or holds it.

seoTitle: Idempotent Import Execution and Record Outcomes
seoDescription: Applies a frozen, validated change set to production state and keeps every record's outcome. See how complete, partial and failed results are separated.

seoTitle: Partial Import Recovery and Resume Journey Example
seoDescription: Only the records that did not land should be touched again. Follow how the failed scope is isolated, corrected and resumed without disturbing the rest.

seoTitle: Migration Readiness and Source-to-Target Mapping
seoDescription: Proving the target can carry the source's meaning before anything moves. Review the source-to-target mapping and the readiness checks that gate the plan.

seoTitle: Migration Execution and Population Verification
seoDescription: Moves the population into the target, then proves the result still means what the source meant. Examine the copy, transform and verification steps.

seoTitle: System Cutover, Observation and Rollback Journey
seoDescription: Switching which system is authoritative happens once, with a way back defined up front. Follow the observation window and the stabilise or roll back call.

seoTitle: Historical Backfill Without Replaying Stale Actions
seoDescription: Repairing a gap in the record without re-enacting what those events would have caused. See how the backfill window is scoped and then applied safely.

seoTitle: Data Transformation Error Recovery Journey Example
seoDescription: Undoing a wrong data change without undoing the right things that came after. Review the reconciliation and the correct, roll forward or roll back paths.

seoTitle: Decision Request Intake and Routing Journey Example
seoDescription: Establishes that authorised judgment is genuinely required and opens a case with a stated scope. Follow the validation and the route, reject or hold exits.

seoTitle: Assigning a Decision Case to an Authorised Reviewer
seoDescription: Putting a case in front of someone actually authorised to decide it. This flow makes reviewer ownership explicit and covers reassignment and escalation.

seoTitle: Evaluating Evidence to Reach an Authorised Decision
seoDescription: How sufficient evidence turns into an authorised decision inside the scope the reviewer holds, and when the case goes back for more information instead.

seoTitle: Collecting Missing Information Before a Decision
seoDescription: Pausing a decision for the fact it is actually missing, without losing the review already done. Follow the collect, revalidate and resume sequence here.

seoTitle: Approved Decision Execution and Revalidation Path
seoDescription: An authorisation still has to apply to what it was granted against. This flow revalidates the target at execution, then executes, holds or invalidates.
reviewReason: Close neighbour of DEC-188, which also revalidates an approval before use; DEC-185 revalidates the target at execution while DEC-188 tests the approval's own validity boundaries.

seoTitle: Recording a Rejection and the Requester's Options
seoDescription: Treats a refusal as the business outcome it is. The reason is recorded and the requester is pointed to remediation, to closure or to a route to reapply.

seoTitle: Splitting Scope After a Partial Approval Decision
seoDescription: Separates the authorised and unauthorised halves of one request so only the approved part can move, and shows how the remaining scope is then resolved.

seoTitle: Approval Validity, Expiry and Revalidation Journey
seoDescription: At the moment of use, is the approval still one? This flow revalidates it in time, context and count, then permits use, expires it or reopens the review.
reviewReason: Close neighbour of DEC-185, the approval execution journey; both gate an approval at the point of use, this one on the approval's own validity boundaries.
